case_assessment.summary: The graph captures the main accident logic reasonably well: ignitable vapor-air mixture in a confined tank, static accumulation in low-conductivity VM&P naphtha, likely spark generation at the gauging float linkage, and resulting internal tank explosion. The main improvements are to make the hazard evidence schema-compliant, clarify the mechanical failure node as the actual linkage separation event rather than only a design weakness, and optionally add the shared operational precursor of stop-start turbulent transfer that the report says contributed to both static buildup and linkage separation.
main_problems: H1 uses paraphrased evidence instead of a direct quote from the incident text.
Ev2 is phrased and evidenced more like a latent design vulnerability than the actual mechanical failure event that occurred during filling.
The common operational precursor of turbulence/bubbling during stop-start transfer pumping is not explicitly represented, so the upstream cause of both Ev1 and Ev2 is compressed.
